# AgentCake

> AgentCake is open-source, self-hosted session replay that tells humans from AI agents. It shows which visits to a website were humans, AI agents or bots, names the agent (Claude in Chrome, Comet, ChatGPT agent, Playwright, Selenium and others), marks when a human and an agent took turns, and gives each session its replay and the reasons for its verdict. One Python process, one SQLite database, no telemetry, MIT licence.

AgentCake answers questions such as: how do I detect AI agents visiting my website, can a website detect Claude in Chrome, how do I tell humans from AI agents in my analytics, and is there bot and agent analytics I can host myself. It records and explains; it does not block or challenge visitors. Every verdict is made on the user's own computer or server, and no AI service is called.

An agent that moves and types like a human, with no name and no trace, can pass as a human; the README gives the current accuracy numbers.

To install it, a coding agent follows INSTALL.md one command at a time and then gives the user the local page, http://127.0.0.1:7878/. A public website's visitors need AgentCake on a server, as SERVER.md describes.

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-behavior-analysis/v0.4.0/README.md): what AgentCake shows, how to install it and how it decides
- [Install](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-behavior-analysis/v0.4.0/INSTALL.md): instructions for an AI coding assistant, one command per step
- [Questions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-behavior-analysis/v0.4.0/docs/FAQ.md): detecting AI agents, Claude in Chrome, accuracy, privacy and how it differs from other tools
- [Server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-behavior-analysis/v0.4.0/SERVER.md): running AgentCake for a public website's visitors, with Docker or systemd
- [Privacy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-behavior-analysis/v0.4.0/PRIVACY.md): what is recorded, where it is kept and how to delete it
